chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Razin, who said:

Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih handed over to me some dirhams from the zakat to distribute. So I came to him one day and he asked me, 'Did you distribute them?' So I said, 'No'. So he made me listen to words wherein was some harshness. So I dropped what remained with me from the dirhams and I arose in anger. So he said to me, 'Return, until I narrate to you something which I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)'. So I returned. So he said, 'I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When I find my zakat, I take it out and hand it over to one whom I trust to distribute it'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with that. Indeed, he is one of the givers'.
Salih said, 'So I took the dirhams when I heard the hadith, and I distributed them'.

key_terms.أَحَدُ الْمُعْطِينَ: One of the givers (participants in reward)

ai.seo_question: Can I give my zakat to someone else to distribute on my behalf?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia legal principle of delegating zakat distribution to a trustworthy agent (muqassim), emphasizing that the trustee shares in the spiritual reward as a co-donor. The Imam’s confirmation that the trustee is 'one of the givers' underscores the continuity of reward through agency, a concept rooted in the broader Shia jurisprudence of trust (amanah) and the merit of charitable intermediaries.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Salih Bin Razeyn who said,

‘Shahab Bin Abd Rabbih handed over some Dirhams from the Zakat to me to distribute them. So I came over to him one day, and he asked me, ‘Did you distribute them?’ So I said, ‘No’. So he made me listen to words wherein was harshness. So I dropped what had remained with me from the Dirhams, and I arose in anger. So he said to me, ‘Return, until I narrate to you with something which I heard from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>’. So I returned. So he said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When I find my Zakat, so can I take it out and hand it over to one who is reliable with it to distribute it?’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is no problem with that. But, he would be one of the givers’.
Salih said, ‘So I took the Dirhams when I heard the Hadeeth, and I distribute them’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Salih ibn Razin who has said the following:

“Shihab ibn ‘ Abd Rabbihi gave to me a certain amount of dirhams of zakat to distribute among the needy. One day I visited him, and he asked, ‘Did you distribute them?’ I said, ‘No, I have not done so.’ He said something that I did not like. I then threw to him what still was not distributed and got up to leave. He said, ‘Come back and allow me to tell you about something that I heard from Ja’far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’ I returned and he said to me, ‘I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, “Can I give the amount of zakat I owe to someone I trust so he can distribute among the needy?” He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is just fine. He receives a reward like the donors of charity.
Salih has said, “I then took the dirhams back after hearing the Hadith, and distributed them (among the needy).”’”
